DY4a6FMkopf.content: The Republican Megabill's SNAP cuts are hitting under-resourced families hard — and we're seeing it firsthand in the Washington, DC Metro region. Since the bill was signed into law on July 4, 2025, SNAP participation has fallen sharply across the country. The @centeronbudget has built a powerful state-by-state tracker showing exactly who is losing coverage and where (link in bio). In the DMV, the data tells a stark story. SNAP participation has fallen 13% in Virginia. In DC, we anticipate a 10–15% decrease in the coming months as additional cuts and work requirements take effect this summer. All of our farmers markets accept SNAP, and our dollar-for-dollar incentive match, FreshMatch, offers up to $30 per day. Despite that, SNAP spending at our markets is down 21% from January through April 2026 compared to the same period last year. That drop has real consequences: ➡️ Shoppers who lost SNAP benefits face reduced access to fresh, local food — often replaced by nothing at all. ➡️ Shoppers with reduced benefits face harder choices, often steering toward cheaper, less nutritious options. ➡️ Farmers and food producers lose revenue from both SNAP and FreshMatch sales, weakening regional food security. FRESHFARM is fortunate to operate other food access programs — including Produce Plus, in partnership with @DCHealth — that provide additional pathways to fresh food. But no local program can fully absorb the impact of federal policy changes of this magnitude. The harm to individuals, families, farmers, and the local food economy is real and growing. 📣 For those working in food systems and food access: what are you seeing in your communities? Share in the comments. #SNAPBenefits #SNAPCuts #foodsecurity #FoodSystem #FoodAccess #FRESHFARMDC #SNAPmatters

DY7FQjBlVED.content: Over 200,000 people in Cuyahoga County receive SNAP benefits to help provide for their families. Now the rules are changing... Under new federal requirements, many adults ages 18-54 must show they are working, in a job training program, in school, or volunteering for at least 80 hours per month to continue receiving benefits. If they don't meet the requirement, they could lose SNAP benefits. These changes are part of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which was passed by Republicans in Congress and signed into law by President Trump.(See why you need to vote) Do you believe able-bodied adults should be required to work, volunteer, or participate in training programs to receive SNAP benefits? A lot of people still have no idea these changes are coming. Share this post so people know what's changing before it affects them. #ClevelandWithCuz #ClevelandNews #SNAPBenefits #BigBeautifulBill

DZPz9DwjWUL.content: Illinois expects up to 150,000 people to lose food stamps this week alone. It is happening in every state in America. Trump's One Big Beautiful Bill expanded SNAP work requirements to adults up to age 64, eliminating exemptions that previously protected veterans, homeless people, and rural residents without access to employment. The new rule requires 80 hours of documented work, schooling, or volunteering every month to stay eligible. If you cannot prove it, you lose your benefits. States are already seeing the consequences. Louisiana has lost 20 percent of all SNAP beneficiaries according to the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities. Tennessee is down nearly 16 percent. Virginia down nearly 15 percent. California food banks are serving 6 million people per month -- more than during COVID. State agencies are overwhelmed. Some cannot process the volume of terminations in time to notify people before their benefits are cut off. Parents of children over the age of 14 are now subject to work requirements for the first time. Food banks are already at pandemic demand levels. And the cuts are just getting started. Follow @updatenow.ai -- news without the filter. #SNAP #FoodStamps #Illinois #BigBeautifulBill

DZQBri4jdOO.content: Trump said it in the State of the Union with pride: "We lifted 2.4 million Americans off food stamps." Here is what he did not say about how he lifted them. Trump's One Big Beautiful Bill cut $186 billion from SNAP over ten years -- the largest cut to any food assistance program in US history, according to Harvard Kennedy School. The Congressional Budget Office confirmed that 2.4 million fewer people receive SNAP each month as a direct result of the bill. They did not find better jobs. They did not improve their circumstances. They lost their eligibility. The CBO also analyzed the full bill's impact by income. The finding: the lowest-income households will see their incomes fall. The richest households will receive a notable income bump. Both effects come from the same legislation. Food banks across the country are already serving clients at COVID pandemic demand levels. The California food bank network is feeding 6 million people per month -- more than at the height of COVID. And the cuts are still being implemented. He called it a win. 2.4 million people call it hunger. Follow @updatenow.ai -- news without the filter. #SNAP #FoodStamps #Trump #CBO
